messages:
eli: FYI we got two enterprise tickets asking for streaming function/tool calls + structured output streaming. both from customers hitting UI latency and memory limits.

maya: which customers? priority?

eli: acme-payments (large merchant) and helios-ml (analytics). acme wants partial tool results streamed to UI for faster UX; helios needs structured fields emitted incrementally to avoid buffering huge JSONs. both blocked on our current non-streaming function call path.

tomas: acme is in late-stage PO negotiations. they asked for a demo by end of Q1 to sign the contract. helios is smaller but vocal in slack. sales view: acme = high ARR risk if we can't show workable plan.

maya: ok. quick triage: we need proposal for scope + launch criteria. sasha can you sketch engineering constraints?

sasha: quick thoughts: streaming completions already supports token streaming. function calls today are delivered only at end-of-response as a complete JSON. two main work items: 1) runtime + protocol changes to emit function call frames as they flush, 2) SDK/contract changes to represent partial function payloads and finalization event.

sasha: we also need to define semantics: are we allowing partial JSON chunks (i.e., arbitrary byte chunks) or delimited logical messages (nl-delimited JSON, or separate 'frame' objects)? tradeoffs for parsing and safety.

raj: infra notes: streaming > increments to connection counts and long-lived sockets. need to validate our LB timeouts and pod connection limits. also watch memory for huge streaming sessions. suggest opt-in header to avoid changing default behavior.

maya: propose opt-in header X-Redwood-Stream-Functions=true and a new streaming frame envelope with types: "partial", "tool_end", "error", "meta". acceptance criteria: backward-compatible (non-opt-in clients unchanged), SDK exposable streams, final tool result identical to current function call output when concatenated.

eli: support asks for clear fallback: if client doesn't support stream frames, fall back to old behavior automatically. customers need SDK snippets.

sasha: MVP idea: NL-delimited JSON frames with envelope {"t":"partial","name":"get_user","payload":"..."} and final frame {"t":"tool_end","name":"get_user","payload":"{...}","complete":true}. parser in SDK stitches partials. no schema validation in MVP.

maya: timeline? estimate for MVP engineering + SDK + docs + basic e2e tests?

sasha: rough split: runtime changes (~2w), SDK updates across python/js (~1w), e2e + infra adjustments (~1w), docs + examples (~.5w). total ~4.5 weeks. stretch for unexpected perf.

raj: need one-week runway for infra rollout and canary to monitor socket saturation and per-conn latency. add telemetry keys: stream_sessions, avg_frame_latency, frame_error_rate.

tomas: relay that to acme: demo timeline 6 weeks acceptable? they'll want early preview.

maya: decision: mark P1 for acme path (opt-in), P2 for feature parity work (schema validation, tooling). action items: sasha owns eng epic, raj infra checklist, eli writes support playbook + customer notes, maya PM coordinates demo + release criteria.

eli: support playbook notes: how to detect client partial parsers failing, fallback guidance, sample SDK usage for react streaming UI. will draft.

sasha: one more technical caveat: function calls that invoke external tool networks may return interleaved logs/streamed events. MVP will forward tool stdout as additional "partial" frames but we should define rate limits and max frame sizes.

maya: launch criteria checklist (initial):
- Opt-in header supported and stable
- SDKs expose stream iterator with stitched function payload
- Final stitched payload matches non-streaming behavior in 99.9% of tests
- Canary across regions with telemetry showing no socket saturation
- Support playbook + demo runbook ready

maya: if all good, GA plan: 6 weeks window, docs + blog post + migration guide. label as incubating feature.

eli: for customers: offer preview flag + engineering contact. recommend enabling preview for acme demo.

tomas: I'll confirm with acme and push for preview access.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created epic #INF-1245 "streaming function call frames (opt-in)" assigned to sasha.

maya: next sync: wednesday 10am to agree on API envelope and SDK contract. please add any missing risks to the epic.

sasha: adding security note: partial payloads must not leak sensitive arguments in logs. will add sanitize hooks and config for redaction.

eli: adding request to epic: include sample react streaming UI in product examples folder. customers like copy-paste demos.

maya: great. closing for now, will send summary + assigned owners. thanks everyone.
